title: UpCheck Aviation Details Custom Avionics and Interactive Cabin for UGF700 in X-Plane 12
summary: A new large-cabin business jet project is taking shape for X-Plane 12, with developer UpCheck Aviation revealing ambitious plans for its UGF700, an unofficial Gulfstream G700-inspired aircraft featuring custom-coded avionics, advanced flight management systems and a highly interactive passenger cabin.
body:
# UpCheck Aviation Reveals UGF700 Business Jet for X-Plane 12 with Custom Avionics and Interactive Cabin

**1 November 2026 | NEWS | X-Plane 12**

Recent development updates provide an insight into the project's progress, with several flight management, communications and cabin functions already reported as implemented.

**UGF700 First Look:** [https://youtu.be/iiTnU-FfVOU](https://youtu.be/iiTnU-FfVOU)

## A New Business Jet for X-Plane 12

The UGF700 is being developed as a detailed representation of a modern ultra-long-range business jet, with particular emphasis on aircraft systems, cockpit functionality and the passenger experience.

Unlike projects relying primarily on X-Plane's default avionics, UpCheck Aviation says it is developing its own avionics architecture, including custom Primary Flight Displays (PFD), Multi-Function Displays (MFD), Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS), and Flight Management System (FMS).

The aircraft is also planned to feature touchscreen controllers for flight management, radios and aircraft systems.

Importantly, the UGF700 is an independent, unofficial project and is not affiliated with Gulfstream Aerospace.

![](</assets/G700 N412AX.jpg>)

## Custom Flight Management and Avionics

UpCheck Aviation's development plans include a comprehensive range of flight management and navigation features.

These include:

- Custom FMS with lateral and vertical navigation.
- Holding patterns and vertical navigation step climbs and descents.
- Missed approach and procedure-turn functionality.
- SimBrief flight-plan integration.
- Take-off and landing performance calculations, including V-speeds, runway requirements and reduced-thrust operations.
- Head-up display with synthetic and enhanced vision.
- Synthetic vision on the Primary Flight Display.
- Integrated charts, electronic flight bag and maintenance pages.

In a development-status update published on 1 November 2026, the developer reported that FMS holding patterns and VNAV step climbs and descents were complete.

Missed approaches and procedure turns were listed as partially implemented, while automatic pausing at the top of descent remains planned.

These statuses reflect the developer's own progress reports and should not be interpreted as independent confirmation that all functions have been fully tested.

## Advanced Communications and VATSIM Integration

Another interesting aspect of the UGF700 is its planned datalink and communications functionality.

According to the developer's latest feature-status report, several functions have already been implemented, including:

- CPDLC communications through Hoppie, alongside SimBrief integration.
- ATC datalink logon.
- Company telex and pre-departure clearance functionality.
- METAR weather requests.

The developer notes that some completed functions still require additional testing or refinement.

VATSIM message integration through an xPilot bridge is partially implemented, while further features, including RealOps integration, remain on the development wishlist.

These systems could make the UGF700 particularly appealing to virtual business aviation pilots who regularly operate on the VATSIM network.

## An Interactive Luxury Passenger Cabin

**UGF700 Cabin First Look:** [https://youtu.be/b-EBSGLZpWU](https://youtu.be/b-EBSGLZpWU)

UpCheck Aviation is also placing considerable emphasis on the aircraft's passenger accommodation.

Development footage released on 25 October showcased the cabin interior, while additional screenshots demonstrated different cabin lighting configurations.

The developer's latest progress report lists several cabin functions as completed, including interactive tables, window blinds, cabin lighting scenes and electronic flight bag controls.

Even the aircraft's shower, vanity facilities and toilet flushing are reported as functional.

Passenger entertainment screens are partially implemented, while additional features such as animated passengers and a star-effect ceiling have not yet been completed.

The attention being given to the passenger cabin suggests that UpCheck Aviation intends to deliver an experience extending well beyond the flight deck.

![](</assets/G700 Lighting 2.jpg>)

## Aircraft Doors and Ground Operations

The developer has also reported progress on ground-handling features.

Main entry-door logic and ground equipment are marked complete, while the baggage door remains partially implemented.

Additional features, including walkaround inspections and expanded airport functionality through the EFB, are not yet implemented.

## First Virtual Airline Partnership

On 1 November 2026, UpCheck Aviation also announced its first official virtual airline partnership with Axiom.

The business aviation virtual airline reportedly has approximately 220 pilots operating through Axiom America and Axiom Europe.

Axiom intends to incorporate the UGF700 into its long-haul virtual business aviation operations once the aircraft becomes available.

The partnership does not establish a release timetable but demonstrates growing interest in the project among virtual aviation operators.

## Release Date and Pricing

UpCheck Aviation has confirmed that the UGF700 is intended to be a paid add-on for X-Plane 12.

However, no price or release date has been announced.

The developer has also stated that beta testing arrangements have not yet been decided.

Given the range of features still under development, it would be premature to speculate about when the aircraft might become available.

## BizJet Pilot's View

The UGF700 is an interesting addition to the growing selection of business aviation projects being developed for X-Plane 12.

Its emphasis on custom avionics, detailed flight management, datalink communications and passenger cabin functionality makes it a project worth watching.

While the aircraft remains in development and several systems are still incomplete, UpCheck Aviation's published progress reports and demonstration videos provide encouraging evidence of work across multiple areas of the aircraft.

BizJet Pilot will continue monitoring the project as further development milestones, screenshots and videos become available.
